text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- China and United States sign new textile agreement, but U.S. penalties of US$19 million against illegal trans-shipments of Chinese textiles remained in place.
- Singapore consortium comprising Port of Singapore Authority and Sembawang Maritime Ltd to help develop Cigading port in West Java, Indonesia, into container terminal.
- Nigerian conmen who have hit businessmen in Singapore several times over the past few years have new scams going.
- Taipei imposes curfew on teenagers under 18 from midnight on Sunday.
- Hong Leong Group will start work on two billion-dollar mixed property developments by early next year, executive chairman Kwek Leng Beng says.
- Personal computer maker IPC Corp faces potential liabilities of only S$24 million in relation to beleagured Korean subsidiary, IPC says.
- IPC Corp group chairman Patrick Ngiam says "IPC Corp is definitely not going under."
- Business performance remained weak in fourth quarter but sentiment improved somewhat, suggesting a weak pickup in first-half 1997.

- With U.S. economy continuing to grow without showing any inflationary pressures, most observers predict Federal Reserve will not change interest rates or tighten monetary policy at a meeting this week.
- Creative Technology shares expected to soar following Saturday's announcement of 111-percent Christmas quarter net profit jump.
- Strong initial public offer sentiment which New Year ushered in shows no sign of receding, with almost all new issues trading at premiums of 20-60 percent to their issue price.
- Indian cabinet likely to reconsider later this month fate of proposed joint venture between India's Tata Group and Singapore Airlines.
